text:
marie: Quick q — planning to work remotely from Lyon for ~6 weeks (Jun 8 - Jul 20). I'll stay on UK payroll. Two quick things: 1) how does the WFH stipend get prorated for a 6‑week temporary move? 2) can I get a one‑off shipping reimbursement for a monitor/stand? Any tax/social security gotchas I should flag? :wave:

alex (People Ops): Thanks for flagging! Short answer: we usually allow short-term remote stints on home payroll but need the temporary remote declaration. Please fill the `Temporary Remote Form` (link below) with exact dates + local address. Stipend is prorated weekly; shipping is handled as a one-off reimbursement up to policy limits.

Form: https://redwood.internal/hr/temporary-remote (submit with receipts) :memo:

carmen - payroll: Marie — before approving we need the exact dates and confirmation you won't be performing work via a French entity or subcontractor. We'll run a tax/nexus screen. For stays under 90 days it's often ok to remain on UK payroll, but France can have specific social security registration triggers depending on employer obligations. Send dates asap.

marie: Thanks — submitting now. One follow-up: is the stipend taxable in the UK or treated as an expense reimbursement? Trying not to trigger unexpected tax withholding.

alex (People Ops): Good Q. Stipend is normally taxable income if paid as regular monthly allowance. For short-term moves we sometimes pay a reimbursed shipping expense (non-taxable with receipts) + a prorated convenience allowance that is taxable. We'll confirm exact tax treatment after payroll/legal review.

joe (Eng): FYI I did a 5‑week split to Spain last year — IT shipped my monitor and we submitted receipts, payroll did a small payroll code change but no huge withholding. VAT on cross-border shipping was the annoying part. If you need IT involved tag them `#it-relocations`.

marie: Submitted the form — hr-bot confirmation below. Added dates and local address.

hr-bot: marie submitted Temporary Remote Declaration (id: TR-2025-789). Receipt upload pending.

carmen - payroll: Got the form. I've queued a tax-nexus check. Provisional stance: stipend estimate £120/week prorated for 6 weeks = £720 taxable; shipping reimbursement up to £250 non-taxable with receipts. Will confirm by EOD Tue.

danielle (Legal): Marie — quick legal note: France has various thresholds for local obligations. While 42 days is typically under many employer-registration triggers, it still depends on the nature of the work and where clients are located. Do not sign any local contracts or invoice from a French bank/account while on this trip. Also please take travel/occupational insurance for work-related activities.

marie: Great — will not set up local bank or accounts. Will upload receipts to the form and CC IT for shipping. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:

alex (People Ops): We'll follow up once payroll and legal sign off. If anything changes (e.g., trip extends past 90 days) please notify us at least 7 days before the extension. We'll also add a short internal note on your UK payroll record: `short-term remote — France (Lyon) Jun8-Jul20` so benefits/payroll teams are aware.

carmen - payroll: Internal note added. Leaving PS: if HR approves a non-taxed shipping reimbursement, send receipts to payroll@redwood.com with subject `TR-2025-789 shipping`.

marie: Thanks everyone — will upload receipts tonight and ping IT.

alex (People Ops): Perfect. Closing loop soon. :eyes:
